title: The Reference Sample Had Changed — Post-Transplant Forensic DNA Chimerism Across Blood (100% Donor), Buccal Swabs (Mixed Leukocyte Infiltration) & Hair/Eyebrow Follicles

teenKit.tldr: A life-saving bone marrow transplant can turn a patient into a genetic shapeshifter, where their blood matches the donor while their hair keeps their original DNA. This creates a forensic mystery when different body parts tell completely contradictory stories about who someone is.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It completely shatters the assumption that a single DNA test is an unchanging permanent truth, forcing both medicine and crime labs to rethink how we identify people.
keyTakeaways: Allogeneic stem cell transplants replace a patient's diseased bone marrow with a donor's healthy stem cells, generating a biological chimerism.
Blood reference samples convert 100% to the donor's genetic profile because blood cells are constantly manufactured by the new bone marrow.
Hair follicles and eyebrow roots remain the most reliable original identity markers because they do not get replaced by donor white blood cells.

vocab.meaning: A biological state where a single living organism possesses tissues with completely different sets of DNA.
A medical procedure where a patient's bone marrow is wiped out and replaced with blood-forming stem cells from a donor.
The natural movement of white blood cells out of the bloodstream and into various tissues like the inside of the cheek.
A genetic testing method that analyzes specific repeating DNA sequences to create a unique molecular fingerprint for identification.

quiz.question: If a male patient receives a bone marrow transplant from a female donor, what will a standard blood DNA test show months later?
options: A 50/50 mix of male and female DNA
Completely female DNA matching the donor
Completely male DNA matching the original patient
quiz.explanation: Because blood cells are constantly manufactured by the newly transplanted bone marrow, the blood profile completely converts to the donor's sex and DNA.

quiz.question: Why do cheek swabs (buccal swabs) often yield a messy, mixed DNA profile after a bone marrow transplant?
options: Cheek cells mutate rapidly when exposed to air
Donor white blood cells migrate out of blood vessels and into the tissue of the cheek
The swab contaminates the sample with skin bacteria
The patient's original DNA actively attacks the swab
quiz.explanation: Leukocyte trafficking brings donor immune cells into mucosal tissues like the cheek, mixing the recipient's cheek cells with the donor's white blood cells.

quiz.question: Which part of the body is safest to test if forensic investigators need a transplant recipient's original, pre-transplant DNA?
quiz.explanation: Hair shafts and eyebrow follicles are isolated from blood circulation and immune cell infiltration, keeping the recipient's original genetic code intact.
